news.title: Argentina star hit with one of the biggest bans in World Cup history
news.lede: Argentina's Leandro Paredes hits Gavi of Spain after the World Cup final. (Getty Images: Marvin Ibo Guengoer). Argentina's Leandro Paredes has been banned from playing for Argentina for 10 matches. Argentina defender Nahuel Molina was also handed a seven-match ban, while Thiago Almada was banned for one.

news.title: FIFA hand down massive penalties to Argentina in bitter fallout to World Cup tournament
news.lede: Three Argentina players have been banned for their part in a brawl at the end of last month’s World Cup final against Spain, along with one Spanish player. Midfielder Leandro Paredes has been hit hardest and given a 10-match ban and a $90,000 ($A125,000) fine by FIFA’s disciplinary committee, while defender Nahuel Molina was given a seven-match suspension and fined the same amount. Thiago Almada was given a one-match ban and a $30,000 ($A42,000) fine, while Argentina coach Roberto Ayala, who had apologised for his part in the altercation, was banned for three matches and fined the same amount. Spain’s Gavi has also been given a one-match ban and a $30,000 ($A42,000).

news.title: BREAKING: FIFA drops biggest punishment in World Cup history
news.lede: Four Argentina players have been suspended after FIFA handed down heavy sanctions for the ugly fight that followed their World Cup final loss to Spain. Football’s governing body announced in the days following the final, which Spain won 1-0 for their second title, that they were undertaking a disciplinary investigation after several La Albiceleste players reacted to defeat by sparking a stoush with their Spanish counterparts after the final whistle. news.title: Gianni Infantino 'plotted U15s World Cup hosted next to DISNEYLAND with 211 teams representing every Fifa nation'
news.lede: GIANNI INFANTINO reportedly tried to launch an Under-15s World Cup next to Disneyland featuring all 211 Fifa nations. The under-fire Fifa chief is said to have plotted a youth “festival of football” inspired by Little League in baseball. Infantino – who is already facing calls to resign after trying to sell off chunks of the World Cup – was hoping to commercialise the U15 tournament. The event would have taken place at the ESPN Wide World Of Sports Complex close to Disneyworld in Orlando, Florida, according to the Athletic.

news.title: FIFA sanctions Argentina and several players for World Cup final scuffle
news.lede: FIFA banned three Argentina players on Friday, including a 10-match suspension for midfielder Leandro Paredes, for striking Spain opponents after losing the World Cup final.
